Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the run chase! The sun is shining brightly, and this will bake the wicket, making it a bit easier for batting. However, we saw the Windies pacers still get some movement, and the Aussies can expect that, especially with the new ball. Kraigg Brathwaite, hoping to make amends for the duck in the first innings, walks out alongside John Campbell to open for West Indies. Mitchell Starc to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

West Indies started well with the new ball as Jayden Seales struck early, removing both Aussie openers. Alzarri Joseph got the nightwatchman, but the bowlers then lost their way, leaking runs with inconsistent lines and lengths. Justin Greaves picked up two key wickets, including Steve Smith, while Alzarri finished with a couple as well. Yet again, it was Shamar Joseph who stood out, wrapping up the innings with a superb four-for. Now, it’s up to the Windies batters to show grit and keep the series alive.

Game in the Balance! Australia would’ve hoped for a few more runs, but they'll still believe they’ve got enough to defend. Steve Smith anchored the innings brilliantly with a composed 71, once again proving why he remains the cornerstone of this Aussie batting line-up. Cameron Green silenced a few doubters with a hard-fought half-century at number 3, while handy knocks from Travis Head and Alex Carey have kept them in a fairly strong position heading into the next phase.

PITCH REPORT - Daren Ganga is pitchside. He says the conditions are overcast, and we can expect one or two interruptions. He says that there is a lot of wear and tear on this wicket and there are a lot of bare patches from the River-end, especially. He mentions that West Indies pacers bowled 10 percent of deliveries finishing on stumps in the starting session, but then they ended the Day with the number reaching 21 percent. He tells that the variable bounce has troubled all the batters in this game, and it should again be a troubling factor for batters on Day 4. He finishes off by saying that batters need to find a way to bat and target their scoring regions.

While we wait, let's hear what Jayden Seales of West Indies has to say. He says that he felt really good and bowled economically and put pressure despite not getting the wickets. Adds that the plan was to get early wickets, but the middle session did not go their way. Says that they decided to attack the stumps in the last session, as there was uneven bounce and they wanted to exploit that. Mentions that Ravi Rampaul has been great, and he knows each and every bowler. Ends by saying that they know that Australia have a good bowling attack, but if they keep out the new ball, they can chase the total down.

UPDATE - Great news! The rain has stopped now, and the covers are coming off too. A few of the players are out there doing some light warm-up drills as well. We are not far away from the action on Day 4 as PLAY WILL START AT 2 PM GMT.

Things are only going to get difficult for the home side from here on, as firstly they need to wrap up the Aussie batting as quickly as possible, and then they need to bat last on this topsy-turvy wicket, which is becoming unplayable by the minute. However, the West Indies do have a batting lineup that can bat deep. So can they really put up a fight and make a match out of this one? We shall find out.

Yesterday, we saw two masterful knocks from Green and Smith as both of them recorded a partnership of 93 runs for the 4th wicket. With Alex Carey set at the crease and knowing that Cummins and Starc can bat, the Aussies well might be thinking of getting the lead past the 300-run mark. For the West Indies, they didn't have a day to remember yesterday, more so as a result of a combination of their pacers being a touch inconsistent in hitting the right areas as well as due to a determined batting effort from the Aussies, led by the modern-day Test match great, Steve Smith.

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the 2nd Test between the West Indies and Australia. We are going to have an early start today as we lost a few overs yesterday due to rain. However, today the forecast is for a nice and sunny day in Grenada, and one can expect a full day's play today. Australia is currently leading by 254 runs with 3 wickets in hand, and it is safe to say that they are in a commanding position at this point in the game. All thanks to their batters, as apart from their openers, all other batters in the top 7 have recorded a combined tally of more than 50 runs each in this game. One might wonder why we are emphasizing such a low run tally, but given how the wicket here has played, every run seems to be worth its weight in gold. This wicket here in Grenada has had consistent seam movement and variable bounce almost throughout the game, and it is expected to further deteriorate on Day 4 and Day 5.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, a stop-start Day 3 comes to an end, but it’s Australia who have edged ahead in this 2nd Test. They’ll look to tighten their grip further by adding another 50–100 runs, if not more, to the lead. With plenty of time lost due to rain, Day 4 will have a scheduled 98 overs to help make up for it, and there’s an early start as well. Play will begin at 1.30 pm GMT, but as always, you can join us beforehand for all the build-up. Cheers!

Steve Smith, the pick of the batters for Australia is up for a quick chat. He says that it is a tricky surface, a bit up and down, with a little bit of seam movement. He adds that as a result, he decided to bat on middle stump and stay still and negate the lbw as much as possible. He also tells that he tried to use the full face of his bat as much as possible. He mentions that he tried to latch on to anything loose. Adds that his first ball hit him straight on his finger, and it was not ideal, but now he feels alright. Further adds that they are in a good position with a lead of over 250, and the pitch is not going to get any better for batting. He finishes off by saying it is that kind of surface where some balls can shoot up and batters might have to take a few blows to their body.

Australia’s second-session dominance rolled on as Cameron Green struck a well-made fifty and shared a 93-run stand with Steve Smith. After Green’s dismissal, Travis Head joined forces with Smith, who soon reached his half-century, and together they pushed the lead past 200 with positive intent. However, Bad Light shortened the final session to just 13.3 overs, during which West Indies hit back strongly with Justin Greaves picking up two key wickets, including Smith, while Shamar Joseph removed the dangerous Head. Alex Carey, though, has looked solid once again and, alongside the skipper, will aim to stretch the lead as much as possible when play resumes on Day 4.

Australia had to navigate a testing period early on under overcast skies, and they did so with confidence, losing only the nightwatchman, Nathan Lyon. Steve Smith and Cameron Green then took charge, and while the scoring rate wasn’t high, they remained solid at the crease, offering West Indies no real openings in a rain-extended session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 46 runs and 3 wickets in 13.3 overs! It was a day largely dominated by Australia, though the hosts will take some comfort from their late fightback in the final session. That said, the Aussies remain firmly in control with a 254-run lead and three wickets still in hand. The pitch is only getting tougher to bat on, making the target increasingly challenging. West Indies have a big task ahead and will be desperate to prevent the visitors from stretching the lead beyond 300.

West Indies tried everything - spin, short balls, and constant rotation, but nothing quite worked. It’s not that batting became easier; rather, Australia’s discipline and the hosts’ inconsistent lengths have tilted the game. After Cameron Green’s departure, Steve Smith quickly reached his fifty and shifted gears, while Travis Head continued his solid form. Without taking many risks, the duo pushed the lead past 200. The Aussies will now aim to stretch it closer to 300, while the Windies need fresh energy and sharper tactics to prevent a daunting target. Join us at 8.15 pm GMT (Previous Day) to catch all the exciting action in the final session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 106 runs and 1 wicket in 24 overs! Australia have now dominated the second session on all three days and are well and truly in the driver’s seat in this Test. After a rain-delayed start, the intent to up the scoring rate was clear from the visitors, and both Cameron Green and Steve Smith executed it effortlessly. The pair stitched together a 93-run stand, extending the lead past 150. Green brought up a hard-fought fifty but couldn’t carry on for much longer.

For the Windies, the first task after Lunch will be to break this partnership and open the door for wickets. Aussies, though currently seeming to be in a good position, can’t relax, as we have seen wickets falling in clusters in this game. It will be interesting to see what is in store for us, as we will be back for the post-Lunch session at 5.10 PM GMT.

For WI the only positive in the session was that they kept the run flow in control and didn’t allow the Aussie batters to run away with the lead. The WI pacers, though, stayed away from the stumps for a lot of deliveries, which didn’t help their cause, and now with the ball having gotten older, it might be hard work for the bowlers in the 2nd session. We haven’t seen any signs of spin till now, and West Indies will definitely be bowling it at some point in the next session. The 2nd session on both days has been contrasting in the sense that AUS on the first day did well with the bat, whereas WI didn’t find it easy on Day 2.

SESSION SUMMARY - 57 Runs, 21 Overs, 1 Wicket. That will be Lunch on Day 3, and Aussies will feel they have won this rain-marred session, as they have managed to lose only one wicket in the session, which was of the nightwatchman, Nathan Lyon. Green is probably playing his best knock in this series, having grinded it out in the middle. On the other hand, Smith is now getting into the zone, having gotten a start. Their partnership is now worth 41 and has started to look dangerous.

Drama on the last ball of the session! A big shout for LBW, but it is turned down. Alzarri Joseph seems very interested, but after a lot of thinking, Roston Chase does not take the review. This is banged into the pitch again, on off, angling in, but keeps a touch low. Steve Smith looks to pull it away but this goes under his bat and hits him high on the pads. Ball Tracking shows it is going over the stumps. Good call by Chase not to take the review. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 3!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for Day 3! There are a few dark clouds, but the sun is shining brightly as well, and as it is a weekend, the crowd has come in numbers too. We can see the West Indies players spread out from the huddle and take up their respective field positions. Nathan Lyon and ​​​​Cameron Green are the overnight batters for Australia. Jayden Seales to start proceedings with the ball. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Darren Ganga is pitchside. He says there has been some overnight rain, and the current weather is a little overcast, nice and cool. He mentions that there are footmarks on both sides of the pitch, and he believes that the ball will continue dominating the bat. He adds that yesterday there was evidence of pitch deterioration, with many deliveries staying low. He also tells how spin could be crucial going ahead in the game, as Lyon in particular did get some purchase from the wicket yesterday.

Anderson Phillip of West Indies also shares a few words. He says that the last Test he played was in Australia, and he had to leave that due to injury, but he is happy to be back in the side now. Adds that now he has a lot of games under his belt and has gained more experience. Praises the Windies pacers and says that they have executed the plans excellently against a top side and will look to continue to work on that to bowl them out to a low total. Mentions that, along with the bowling, he has also put in the hard work with the bat and wants to contribute in both facets of the game.

Nathan Lyon of Australia is up for a quick chat. He says his hand is good after he got hit on it yesterday, and he feels it will heal by the 4th innings bowling dig. He mentions that yesterday was pretty challenging, with the ball and Brandon King, especially, batted well with intent and got a good score on a pretty challenging wicket. On two wickets for him and how the surface is, he says that he is excited about the 4th innings, and firstly, he hopes they have a good time with the bat. On being asked about what his teammates feel about his batting, he says Smith wanted him to retire hurt and wanted to come out to bat, but he personally feels he is a good batter, and he is always ready to give it a crack.

Now talking about what might be in store for us on Day 3, well, the wicket has worsened, and with the ball still being new, the first hour will be mighty challenging for the Aussie batters. From the West Indies point of view, it will be an opportunity for them to trigger a collapse and ensure that they chase as low a total as possible. The pitch is already playing upside down, in addition to that, it has also started to turn, and hence, anything over 150 won't be easy to chase on this wicket. The forecast for today does have some rain on the radar, and one would hope the rain gods stay away for as long as possible. Stay tuned as the action is not far away.

Aussie pacers were, as always, accurate with their lines and lengths, but they will rue the fact that they allowed the WI tail to wag. The West Indies were 174/7 at one point, and it seemed like Australia would get a material first innings lead. But thanks to the two Josephs, who stitched together a 51-run stand, as eventually the West Indies got bowled out for a total of 253. The contribution from the West Indies bottom five was crucial not only from a point of view of runs, but also because it ensured that Australia got to bat for a nervous six-over period at the fag end of Day 2. West Indies pacers made merry with the new ball as they sent the two Australia openers in quick succession, as Australia ended the day with a lead of 45 and two wickets down.

Hello and welcome to the 'Moving Day' of this Test. Yes, you guessed it right. We are up and getting ready for Day 3 of the 2nd Test between Australia and West Indies. This game has been moving on a pendulum, where the momentum has been shifting to and fro between both teams. Day 2 started with the West Indies' response as the home side batted positively in the 1st session, albeit losing three wickets. Campbell batted well for his 40. Brandon King showed application at the crease, as he stitched two crucial stands, first with Chase and then with Shai Hope. He eventually got out on 75.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

And that wraps up a thrilling Day 2 of this 2nd Test! All eyes now turn to Day 3, famously known as 'Moving Day', where the match can swing dramatically in either direction. With both Australia and West Indies looking to land the decisive blow, things are perfectly balanced and set up for another gripping day of action. The first ball will be bowled at 2 pm GMT, but do join us earlier for all the pre-match build-up. Until then, cheers!

Floyd Reifer, the batting consultant of West Indies is up for a quick chat. He says that at the beginning of the day, he would have wanted a score over 300 and take a lead of about 50 runs, but he still heaps praises on the batters as he says all batters did well, and everyone chipped in from the top order to the tail enders. On what he is working on with the batters, he mentions that it’s a fairly new batting line up with the likes of John Campbell, Chase, who have been away for quite a bit, and adds that Brandon King is in his debut series. So he feels, these batters need to be given time to get used to Test cricket. On Brandon King’s knock, he says King tried to score off full and short balls and showed good defense as well. Ends by saying that the wicket will deteriorate, and hence he feels something around 200-220 can be chasable in the last innings.

West Indies dominated the final session, first with a vital 51-run eighth-wicket stand between Shamar and Alzarri Joseph, followed by 16 more for the last wicket to trim the deficit to just 33 runs. With momentum on their side, they came out firing with the ball as Jayden Seales delivered a fiery spell, removing both Australian openers in quick time to swing the contest back into balance. Cameron Green and nightwatchman Nathan Lyon managed to survive the tense final overs, ensuring Australia ended the day without further damage.

The hosts couldn’t carry their momentum into the second session, as Australia’s bowlers came out firing and immediately put them on the back foot. Josh Hazlewood struck early once again, breaking the promising partnership right at the start. While Brandon King and Shai Hope briefly revived the innings with a solid stand, with King also reaching a well-deserved half-century, Australia quickly regained control. Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon combined to deliver crucial blows, sharing three key wickets between them and reducing West Indies to 174/7.

West Indies began the day positively with the bat and, much like Australia on Day 1, managed to keep the scoreboard ticking despite losing a few wickets. John Campbell once again couldn’t make his start count, falling in the 40s for the sixth time in his Test career, leaving the visitors in a spot of bother at 64/3. But Brandon King and Roston Chase then dug in, displaying solid application and composure to steady the ship. Their partnership carried West Indies safely to Lunch without further damage, while also pushing the total past the 100-run mark.

SESSION SUMMARY - 80 runs and 5 wickets in 27.2 overs! If Day 1 was full of drama, Day 2 has taken things up a notch! This is the beauty of Test cricket. When both sides go toe-to-toe, the contest becomes all the more compelling. Australia had West Indies on the ropes more than once, but the hosts showed great resilience to claw their way back. Heading into Day 3, they’ll be on the happier side, having reduced the Aussies to an effective lead of just 45 with two wickets already down.

OUT! LBW! THATS AS PLUMB AS IT GETS! Jayden Seales doesn't even bother looking back as he is on a celebratory run. More of a celebrappeal from Stuart Broad's books! This is a full ball that nips back in sharply and stays low too. Khawaja is undone by the movement and the bounce as he fails to bring his bat down in time. The umpire's finger goes up after a moment. Khawaja consults his partner, and with three seconds to go, he signals 'T' to the umpire. Nothing on UltraEdge as the ball passes close to the bat. Ball Tracking coming up. Pitching outside off, impact in line, and wickets hitting. Three reds, and Khawaja has to go. He got out in pretty much a similar way in the 1st innings. Both the Aussie openers are gone now!
